title: Nagoya in 1 Day — Nagoya Castle, Ōsu, Atsuta
subtitle: A same-day round trip with no hotel: Nagoya Castle, Ōsu and Atsuta Shrine
summary: For a layover or a single free day: head into the city from the airport, see Nagoya Castle, the Ōsu shopping arcades and Atsuta Shrine, then return to the airport in the evening. No hotel needed. Inuyama Castle, Horaiken, Oasis 21 and the Sky Promenade are kept as alternates. The notes cover getting to and from the airport, getting around on the day, and what has changed lately.

Travelogue details
The order of stops follows the author's one-day dash in September 2023; the Inuyama Castle and eel rice the author wrote about wanting to try are added as alternates.
What this itinerary is
A one-day dash with no hotel: arrive in the early morning, leave late at night.

The travelogue's author took red-eye flights on a low-cost carrier (out early in the morning, arriving at dawn; back late at night). The timings here are built around that kind of schedule, so go by your own flights.
Low-cost carriers usually limit the number and weight of carry-on bags, so follow the airline's rules; with no checked bag you can travel light for the day.
Entry
Before you leave, register your immigration and customs declaration on Visit Japan Web and show the QR code on arrival: https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp/main/#/vjwpco001
Between the airport and the city

Chubu Centrair Airport to Nagoya Station: the Meitetsu Airport Line limited express (μ-SKY) takes about 30 min; it needs an extra limited-express ticket and you can reserve a seat. Rapid and local trains are cheaper but slower. Check fares on the Meitetsu website.
From the 2023 travelogue: a one-way ticket plus μ-SKY bought online in advance came to about NT$271.
Timetables and fares: https://www.meitetsu.co.jp/eng/
Getting around on the day

The Meijo Line subway is the backbone of the day (Kamimaezu, Shiyakusho, Sakae and Atsuta Jingu Nishi are all on it); a one-day pass is available, so work out whether it pays off for the rides you plan.
Rain is common, so bring an umbrella; there are few shops near Nagoya Castle.
Current conditions
Nagoya Castle's main keep is closed for renovation; you can only visit Honmaru Palace and the gardens.
Ōsu Kannon's main hall was under repair when the travelogue's author visited; check the current state before you go.
Nagoya Castle admission changes from 1 October 2026; go by the official site.
Other
On a late-night flight, watch the last connecting train and the hours when the airport check-in counters open and close.
There is plenty of time on the way back, so browse the duty-free shops at Terminal 1 and watch planes from the observation deck.
